div.div:
optimizer::optimize_both(working) (optimize() wraps it and keeps only the model input and the crop). Two steps, then a control.
1 Colour balance: Levels, once per image. lo = 0.68 percentile, hi = 99.32 percentile (lowest lo / highest hi of the 3 channels), gamma = 1 + lo/(255-lo) - (255-hi)/hi (0.01-9.99), one 256-entry table. Identity table: used as is.
2 Trim, on the balanced image: 16 border samples (4 per edge, at 0/25/50/75%) give the backdrop colour range (min/max per channel). Gaps closed with a 2x2 window. Box around the product, squared to its largest side, grown by max(10 px, 10% of that side); the square is slid inside the frame. Crop.
3 Control, trim 2 (recheck_box): the same trim run again on trim 1's box. Recorded only when a side moved by more than TRIM_RECHECK_TOLERANCE_PX (2). The model never sees it; core::framing reads both boxes.
Nothing left = Err: the file stays in INPUT.

div.div:
optimizer::detect_letterbox(original) → LetterboxReport
Classifies each edge as Backdrop, FlatOther or Varied. An opposite pair FlatOther with the other pair Varied is flat padding bars. If the interior also reads as textured (T_TEXTURE_HIGHPASS), keep = the content rect. trim_letterbox() returns .keep.
Called from preprocessor::preprocess on the full-resolution original; stored in Prepared::letterbox. Wired: shot_classifier::route::decide reads it (R1Job::Reframe) and R1 hands the trimmed part to extend.rs. Two same-coloured bars read as backdrop and are not caught.

Called from core::process_file after classify, not from preprocess.

center_and_stretch (mod.rs)
struct Silhouette { row_x, col_y }
Per original-image row and column, the span [lo, hi) the mask occupies, grown by a disc of the clearance (20 working px scaled up). Lines with no subject take the nearest line's span; no edge moves faster than R1_BAND_SLOPE_PX_PER_LINE.
Silhouette::from_mask(mask, orig_w, orig_h, grow) scales the working-resolution mask up.
On a textured background compose uses it for all four edges, so the untouched product band follows the silhouette, not its bounding box

div.div:
extend.rs · Part C (center_and_stretch/extend.rs)
Re-frame a trimmed textured scene to a square, without R1's background stretch.
Wired: apply calls reframe_to_square for R1Job::Reframe, which shot_classifier::route picks when Prepared::letterbox is set.
1 square_crop_preserving(subject, w, h) — crop a square that keeps the whole subject; None if it cannot.
2 seam_carve_to_square(src, target) — grow each axis by minimum-energy seam insertion; None when the cheapest seams cost more than R1_SEAM_CARVE_MAX_SEAM_ENERGY.
3 white_pad(src) — last resort: centre on a white square.
reframe_to_square tries 1, 2, 3 in that order.

div.div:
flatness.rs · is_flat(original, mask) → rough_share, crease_step
At the mask's size, blocks of R1_FLAT_BLOCK_PX 24 clear of the mask (by the clearance + 3 px); a block is rough when its luma std, slow ramps taken out, is above 2.0. Flat = at most 10% of the blocks rough. Flat → the stretch starts from the subject's box and the gradients run. Textured, or nothing to measure → the grown silhouette's band, no gradients.
crease_step: the 99th percentile of the step between adjacent background luma pixels, high on creased paper.

div.div:
grazes.rs · blocked_lines(mask, flagged edges, orig) → Blocked; Blocked::choose_fill(src, bgc)
For each edge pass 1 flagged: a line is blocked when the mask has a pixel within GATE_MARGIN_PX of the border on it, plus GATE_MARGIN_PX lines either side. A blocked line is not stretched. Edges the gate did not flag are untouched.
Blocked::choose_fill, the second test, per edge with blocked lines: flat (a BGC was found, or the outermost line spans at most R1_GRAZE_FLAT_TOLERANCE 3 levels) → plain colour or ramp; any other edge → patch fill.

div.div:
compose.rs · compose_with_holes(src, plan, silhouette, bgc, flat_box, blocked) → canvas + gap flags (compose wraps it)
Real part laid in a blank square, then stretch_edge once per edge the square overhangs: left, right, top, bottom, the same code for all four. Per line: product band kept (silhouette grown 20 working px, or the subject's box on a flat background); the background beside it stretched evenly over itself plus the overhang, nothing invented. No background (bled) → flat fill, then a blend of the clean lines either side plus measured grain. Blocked lines → a plain ramp, or a gap flag for the patch fill.

right, top, bottom, the same code for all four. Per line: product band kept (silhouette grown 20
working px, or the subject's box on a flat background); the background beside it stretched
evenly over itself plus the overhang, nothing invented. No background (bled) → flat fill, then a
blend of the clean lines either side plus measured grain. Blocked lines → a plain ramp, or a
gap flag for the patch fill.

div.div:
gradients.rs · blend(canvas, square) → bool, flat background only
Five zones fade the invented overhang into one colour: red (bottom), green and yellow (bottom corners), blue and cyan (left, right). A zone exists only on a side the square overhangs. The colour is sampled at the zone's own edge (edge_target: mean of the edge band, then of the outermost line, over the lines the product does not graze); under 10 such lines → the whole-photo median outside the mask. The subject's box is never touched.

text.tspan: gradients.rs · blend(canvas, square) → bool, flat background only
Five zones fade the invented overhang into one colour: red (bottom), green and yellow
(bottom corners), blue and cyan (left, right). A zone exists only on a side the square
overhangs. The colour is sampled at the zone's own edge (edge_target: mean of the edge
band, then of the outermost line, over the lines the product does not graze); under 10 such
lines → the whole-photo median outside the mask. The subject's box is never touched.

patch.rs · fill(canvas, gaps, scene)
Runs after the gradients, on the gap flags compose returned. Clone-stamp style: patches of R1_PATCH_PX 11 are copied from the safe overhang and the real background outside the product and its margin, the gap pixel with the most known neighbours first, best of R1_PATCH_CANDIDATES 4000 sources. Then Poisson healing (conjugate gradients) blends the colours into the surroundings.

div.div: Headcut — only when Options::enable_headcuts. headcut_eligible: not both Left and Right touched. plan_headcut cuts a square section out of the model input and asks maria_antonieta::cut_above_philtrum where to cut. On a white-bars picture headcut_in_bars keeps the bars out and cuts only if the room below the cut is at least 75% of the mask width (HEADCUT_BARS_MAX_SHORTFALL). Cut → peel the picture and re-run the edge judge; no second model run.

div.div:
plan_square(prep, subject, touches) → Option<SquarePlan> (plan.rs)
Square = larger axis need: extent × (1 + 4.2% per free side: 8.4% with two free sides, 4.2% with one, none if bled at both ends). Bled edge pinned (Pins::from_edges); slack to the free sides. CentreContent (core::framing) cuts from the content box instead, no margin.
Some → R1 Stretch(plan). None (no legal square) → R3

two free sides, 4.2% with one, none if bled at both ends). Bled edge

(core::framing) cuts from the content box instead, no margin.
